title: Glueing of schemes along open immersions
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme, let $\{Y_i\to Y\}$ be a Zariski cover, and for
each $i$ let $P_i\to Y_i$ be a scheme. Suppose given isomorphisms
$\varphi_{ij}:P_i\times_YY_j\to P_j\times_YY_i$ over $Y_i\times_YY_j$
with $\varphi_{ii}=\operatorname{id}$ and
$\varphi_{jk}\varphi_{ij}=\varphi_{ik}$ over the triple intersections.
Then there is a $Y$-scheme $P$ with isomorphisms
$P\times_YY_i\cong P_i$ over $Y_i$ compatible with the
$\varphi_{ij}$, unique up to unique isomorphism.

proof.text: Write $b_i:Y_i\hookrightarrow Y$ for the covering open immersions and $f_i:P_i\to Y_i$, $a_i=b_i\circ f_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product], $U_{ij}:=P_i\times_Y Y_j$ is the open subscheme $a_i^{-1}(Y_j)$ of $P_i$. Because $\varphi_{ij}$ is over $Y_i\times_Y Y_j$, it preserves the map to $Y$; consequently it identifies $U_{ij}\cap U_{ik}$ with $U_{ji}\cap U_{jk}$. Indeed both are the inverse image of $Y_k$ in the corresponding overlap. Also $U_{ii}=P_i$, and the cocycle with $k=i$ gives $\varphi_{ji}=\varphi_{ij}^{-1}$. Thus the hypotheses give exactly the open-overlap gluing data, including the domain condition on triple intersections.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes] to $(P_i,U_{ij},\varphi_{ij})$. Obtain a scheme $P$ with covering open immersions $q_i:P_i\to P$, satisfying $q_i|_{U_{ij}}=q_j\circ\varphi_{ij}$ and $q_i(U_{ij})=q_i(P_i)\cap q_j(P_j)$. The maps $a_i$ agree on these overlaps, since the given transition isomorphisms are over $Y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing], there is a unique $p:P\to Y$ with $p\circ q_i=a_i$.

For each $i$, $q_i(P_i)=p^{-1}(Y_i)$. The forward inclusion follows from $p\circ q_i=b_i\circ f_i$. Conversely, write any $x\in p^{-1}(Y_i)$ as $q_j(z)$ using the cover from [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes]. Then $a_j(z)=p(x)\in Y_i$, so $z\in U_{ji}$. The overlap equation gives $x=q_i(\varphi_{ji}(z))$, proving the reverse inclusion. Both $q_i:P_i\to P$ and the inclusion of $p^{-1}(Y_i)$ identify their sources with the open subscheme on this same open subset; the definition [def-weil-open-immersion] therefore identifies $P_i$ with $p^{-1}(Y_i)$ as schemes. This uses equality of open subschemes, rather than an inference about a closed subscheme from its underlying set.

By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product], $p^{-1}(Y_i)$ is $P\times_Y Y_i$. Hence the isomorphism of step 3 gives $P\times_Y Y_i\cong P_i$. Its map to $Y_i$ is $f_i$: after composition with the inclusion $b_i$ both maps are $p\circ q_i$, and an open immersion identifies its source with an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion], so equality can be checked after this inclusion. On the common restriction to $Y_i\cap Y_j$, the change from the $i$-chart to the $j$-chart is precisely $\varphi_{ij}$, since $q_i|_{U_{ij}}=q_j\circ\varphi_{ij}$ in step 2. Thus these are the required compatible isomorphisms over the base opens.

Uniqueness includes the chosen compatible local identifications. Let $(P^{\prime},p^{\prime})$ be another such object, and let $q_i^{\prime}:P_i\to P^{\prime}$ be the inverses of its local identifications followed by the open inclusions. These are covering open immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] and [def-weil-open-immersion]. The maps $q_i^{\prime}\circ q_i^{-1}:q_i(P_i)\to P^{\prime}$ agree on overlaps because both systems have the same transition $\varphi_{ij}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to obtain $h:P\to P^{\prime}$, and apply it in the opposite direction to obtain $k$. The same lemma checks on the respective covering charts that $kh=\mathrm{id}_P$, $hk=\mathrm{id}_{P^{\prime}}$, and $p^{\prime}h=p$. It also says that any map respecting the local identifications equals $h$. This proves existence and uniqueness of the compatible $Y$-isomorphism.

lean.statement: theorem exists_scheme_of_zariski_cocycle (Y : Scheme.{u}) (I : Type v) (Yᵢ Pᵢ : I → Scheme.{u}) (b : ∀ i : I, Yᵢ i ⟶ Y) [∀ i : I, IsOpenImmersion (b i)] (hcover : ∀ y : Y, ∃ (i : I) (x : Yᵢ i), b i x = y) (f : ∀ i : I, Pᵢ i ⟶ Yᵢ i) (φ : ∀ i j : I, pullback (f i ≫ b i) (b j) ≅ pullback (f j ≫ b j) (b i)) (hφ : ∀ i j : I, (φ i j).hom ≫ pullback.fst (f j ≫ b j) (b i) ≫ f j = pullback.snd (f i ≫ b i) (b j) ∧ (φ i j).hom ≫ pullback.snd (f j ≫ b j) (b i) = pullback.fst (f i ≫ b i) (b j) ≫ f i) (hφ_self : ∀ i : I, φ i i = Iso.refl _) (hcocycle : ∀ (i j k : I) (T : Scheme.{u}) (a : T ⟶ pullback (f i ≫ b i) (b j)) (d : T ⟶ pullback (f j ≫ b j) (b k)) (c : T ⟶ pullback (f i ≫ b i) (b k)), a ≫ (φ i j).hom ≫ pullback.fst (f j ≫ b j) (b i) = d ≫ pullback.fst (f j ≫ b j) (b k) → a ≫ pullback.fst (f i ≫ b i) (b j) = c ≫ pullback.fst (f i ≫ b i) (b k) → d ≫ pullback.snd (f j ≫ b j) (b k) = c ≫ pullback.snd (f i ≫ b i) (b k) → d ≫ (φ j k).hom ≫ pullback.fst (f k ≫ b k) (b j) = c ≫ (φ i k).hom ≫ pullback.fst (f k ≫ b k) (b i)) : ∃ (P : Scheme.{u}) (p : P ⟶ Y) (e : ∀ i : I, pullback p (b i) ≅ Pᵢ i), (∀ i : I, (e i).hom ≫ f i = pullback.snd p (b i)) ∧ (∀ i j : I, pullback.fst (f i ≫ b i) (b j) ≫ (e i).inv ≫ pullback.fst p (b i) = (φ i j).hom ≫ pullback.fst (f j ≫ b j) (b i) ≫ (e j).inv ≫ pullback.fst p (b j)) ∧ ∀ (P' : Scheme.{u}) (p' : P' ⟶ Y) (e' : ∀ i : I, pullback p' (b i) ≅ Pᵢ i), (∀ i : I, (e' i).hom ≫ f i = pullback.snd p' (b i)) → (∀ i j : I, pullback.fst (f i ≫ b i) (b j) ≫ (e' i).inv ≫ pullback.fst p' (b i) = (φ i j).hom ≫ pullback.fst (f j ≫ b j) (b i) ≫ (e' j).inv ≫ pullback.fst p' (b j)) → ∃! h : P ≅ P', h.hom ≫ p' = p ∧ ∀ i : I, (e i).inv ≫ pullback.fst p (b i) ≫ h.hom = (e' i).inv ≫ pullback.fst p' (b i)
